facts: The central angle $\theta$ in radians is the ratio of arc length $l$ to radius $r$: $\theta = \dfrac{l}{r}$.
Because radian measure is a ratio of two lengths, it is a **dimensionless** quantity.
One full revolution of $360^{\circ}$ equals $2\pi\text{ radians}$, since $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi r}{r} = 2\pi$.
A straight angle of $180^{\circ}$ equals $\pi\text{ radians} \approx 3.14159\text{ radians}$.
An angle of $\theta\text{ radians}$ subtends an arc containing $\theta$ radius lengths: $l = r\theta$.
The fraction of a circle represented by angle $\theta$ is $\dfrac{\theta}{2\pi}$.

foundation.question_text: State the geometric definition of $1\text{ radian}$ in terms of the radius $r$ and the subtended arc length $l$.
foundation.solution_text: One radian is the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the radius ($l = r$).

foundation.question_text:
The circumference of a circle of radius $r$ is $C = 2\pi r$.
Explain why one complete revolution ($360^{\circ}$) is equal to $2\pi\text{ radians}$.
foundation.solution_text:
The angle in radians is the ratio of arc length to radius:
$\theta = \dfrac{\text{arc length}}{\text{radius}}$
For one complete revolution, the arc length is the circumference $2\pi r$:
$\theta = \dfrac{2\pi r}{r}$
$= 2\pi\text{ radians}$

foundation.question_text:
An arc of length $12\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle $\theta$ at the centre of a circle of radius $4\text{ cm}$.
Find the angle $\theta$ in radians.

A central angle of $4\text{ radians}$ is formed in a circle of radius $r$.
Express the subtended arc length $l$ in terms of $r$.
foundation.solution_text:
An angle of $4\text{ radians}$ means the arc length is $4$ times the radius:
$l = 4r$

foundation.question_text:
A sector of a circle of radius $5\text{ cm}$ has an arc length of $15\text{ cm}$.
Find the angle $\theta$ subtended at the centre in radians.

An arc of a circle represents $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of the full circumference.
Calculate the central angle subtended by this arc in radians, in terms of $\pi$.
foundation.solution_text:
One full revolution is $2\pi\text{ radians}$.
$\theta = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 2\pi$
$= \dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$

foundation.question_text: Explain why radian measure is described as a dimensionless quantity, unlike degrees.
foundation.solution_text:
Radian measure is defined as the ratio of arc length to radius (length $\div$ length).
The units of length cancel out, making a radian a pure dimensionless number.

development.solution_text:
By definition, when the arc length equals the radius ($l = r$), the central angle is $1\text{ radian}$.
$\theta = \dfrac{l}{r} = \dfrac{r}{r} = 1\text{ radian}$

development.question_text: Show that a straight angle (a half turn of $180^{\circ}$) subtends an angle of $\pi\text{ radians}$ at the centre of a circle of radius $r$.
development.solution_text:
A half turn forms a semicircular arc of length $\dfrac{1}{2} C = \pi r$.
$\theta = \dfrac{\text{arc length}}{r}$
$= \dfrac{\pi r}{r}$
$= \pi\text{ radians}$

development.question_text:
A pendulum of length $80\text{ cm}$ swings so that its tip traces an arc of length $20\text{ cm}$.
Find the angle subtended by the swing in radians.

A central angle measures $2.5\text{ radians}$ in a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$.
State how many radius lengths fit along the arc, and calculate the exact arc length.
development.solution_text:
The angle $\theta = 2.5\text{ radians}$ means the arc contains $2.5$ radius lengths.
$l = r\theta$
$= 6 \times 2.5$
$= 15\text{ cm}$

development.question_text:
The ratio of the arc length of a circular sector to the circumference of the circle is $\dfrac{3}{8}$.
Find the central angle $\theta$ in radians, expressed in terms of $\pi$.

An arc of length $7\pi\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle $\theta$ at the centre of a circle of radius $14\text{ cm}$.
Find the exact angle $\theta$ in radians in terms of $\pi$.

A student measures a circular arc as $15\text{ metres}$ on a circle of radius $3\text{ metres}$ and computes $\theta = 5$.
Explain why the unit metres does not appear in the final angle.
development.solution_text:
The calculation is $\theta = \dfrac{15\text{ m}}{3\text{ m}} = 5$.
The linear units of metres in the numerator and denominator divide out, leaving the angle as a pure dimensionless ratio.

mastery.question_text:
A wheel of radius $r$ rolls along a horizontal line without slipping through a distance equal to its circumference $2\pi r$.
Explain why the angle turned by the wheel at its axle is exactly $2\pi\text{ radians}$.
mastery.solution_text:
The distance rolled along the ground equals the arc length of the outer rim that has made contact: $l = 2\pi r$.
The angle turned in radians is the ratio of this arc length to the radius:
$\theta = \dfrac{l}{r}$
$= \dfrac{2\pi r}{r}$
$= 2\pi\text{ radians}$

mastery.question_text:
In a circle of radius $r$, the ratio of the radius to the subtended arc length is $2:5$.
Find the central angle $\theta$ in radians and state the exact fraction of a full revolution it represents.
mastery.solution_text:
Given $\dfrac{r}{l} = \dfrac{2}{5}$, the reciprocal ratio is $\dfrac{l}{r} = \dfrac{5}{2}$.
$\theta = \dfrac{l}{r} = 2.5\text{ radians}$
The fraction of a full revolution ($2\pi$) is:
$\dfrac{\theta}{2\pi} = \dfrac{2.5}{2\pi} = \dfrac{5}{4\pi}$

mastery.question_text:
A point travels around a circle of radius $10\text{ cm}$, covering an arc length equal to the perimeter of a regular hexagon of side length $5\text{ cm}$.
Find the angle subtended at the centre in radians.
mastery.solution_text:
The perimeter of the regular hexagon is:
$l = 6 \times 5 = 30\text{ cm}$
The central angle in radians is:
$\theta = \dfrac{l}{r}$
$= \dfrac{30}{10}$
$= 3\text{ radians}$
